name: Carpus
title: Paul's Hospitality in Troas
summary: Carpus was a Christian in Troas with whom the apostle Paul left his cloak and scrolls. He is mentioned only once in the Bible, in 2 Timothy 4:13. Although little is known about him, Paul's trust in him suggests that he was a reliable believer and an important supporter of the apostle's ministry.

keyEvents.title: Paul Leaves Belongings with Carpus
keyEvents.description: Paul asked Timothy to bring the cloak he had left with Carpus in Troas, along with the books and especially the parchments.

keyEvents.title: Paul's Last Letter to Timothy
keyEvents.description: The mention of Carpus occurs in Paul's last known letter, written from prison in Rome, where he urges Timothy to come to him soon.

keyEvents.title: Troas as an Important Mission Site
keyEvents.description: Troas was a key hub for the early Christian mission, which Paul had visited several times. Carpus was part of the Christian community there.

keyEvents.title: Carpus as a Trusted Friend
keyEvents.description: The fact that Paul left valuable personal belongings with Carpus shows that he was a trusted fellow believer whom Paul relied on in his ministry.
